# Weekly Market Briefing — August 16, 2026

## 1. Market Regime — Cautiously Risk-On
The backdrop is **calm and rate-neutral**. VIX sits at 14.25 (▼2.25 MoM) — the VIX index fell to its lowest level since Dec. 29, signaling minimal hedging demand. The 10Y-3M curve is normal at +1.00 pt (10Y 4.7%, 3M 3.7%), and DXY has softened to 99.67 (▼1.06). Broad-market factor readings lean modestly risk-on: small-caps (IWM Momentum 84) and QQQ (Momentum 73) outrank defensives, though SPY/DIA still carry high Low-Vol scores (64/73), reflecting quality-led leadership rather than junk-rally froth. Notably, MSFT (12-1 momentum −24%) and META (−17%) show mega-cap dispersion beneath calm index surfaces.

## 2. This Week's News
Two soft data prints defined the week. Nonfarm payrolls unexpectedly declined in July, falling by 23,000 amid a drop of 53,000 government jobs, while the unemployment rate edged lower to 4.1%. Wednesday's CPI was benign: headline inflation rose 0.1% month over month and was up 3.4% year over year. Then Friday, July retail sales fell for the first time in nine months, and August consumer sentiment dipped to 51, from 55.2 in July. Markets read this as reducing hike risk: this month's CPI reading, combined with a lackluster July jobs report, may keep hawkish Fed officials at bay in September, though the near-term inflation outlook remains guarded amid volatile oil prices and lingering core pressures. Context: the FOMC decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, on a 9-3 vote, with three members dissenting who wanted to hike. Equities held up — US equities ended with gains for a third straight week, their longest winning streak since May, even as they slipped off record highs Friday on softer consumer data.

## 3. Factor Leadership — Momentum & Energy
**Momentum is being rewarded.** Top ranks cluster in AMD (100), SNOW (98), SHOP (96), and XLK (93). Energy stands out across factors: **XLE** carries Momentum 89, Value 76, and Low-Vol 86 with a 39% 12-1 return — consistent with oil prices rising, adding pressure amid low-volume summer trading. Defensives (XLP Low-Vol 94, XLU 91) remain bid but rank low on momentum, confirming a leadership tilt toward cyclical/growth over pure defense.

## 4. Notable Movers
- **Overbought (RSI>70):** MSFT (71), SNOW (72), SHOP (67 near), AMD-adjacent names. SNOW pairs Momentum 98 with Quality 4 — a speculative combination.
- **Oversold (RSI<30):** XRP (35), TLT (40) — bonds pressured despite tame CPI.
- **Extreme momentum:** AMD's +174% 12-1 return anchors the top; crypto is broadly crushed (DOGE −50.7%, ADA −64%, all 52wH >−66%).
- **Value + Quality:** ABBV (Value 98, Quality 80) and XLF (Value 83) screen well.

## 5. Themes to Watch
Retail earnings dominate next week — retail earnings take center stage, with Target and Walmart among companies scheduled to report — a key read on the consumer after soft sales/sentiment. Then one of the most anticipated reports of the quarter: Nvidia on August 26. Also watch **Jackson Hole** — with the Fed's Jackson Hole conference taking place August 27-29, low VIX could change. Monitor rising oil/Iran headlines, sticky real yields (TLT weak), and whether the softening consumer tips "slowdown" into "recession" concern.
